media.connector: LC Duplex (or SC/APC for Carrier Telco Hand-off)
media.technicalReason: For link distances above 400m (6200.0 km requested), OS2 Single-Mode Fiber (9/125 µm core) eliminates modal dispersion entirely. Core diameter permits only a single fundamental transverse optical mode, enabling high-bandwidth transmission over tens of kilometers. Interface "10GBASE-ZR SFP+ (1550nm Cooled EML / APD Receiver)" was selected to guarantee optical link margin over the required span.
assumptions: Low water-peak ITU-T G.652.D single-mode fiber infrastructure.
Optical attenuation calculated at 1310nm (~0.35-0.4 dB/km) or 1550nm (~0.22-0.25 dB/km).
Receiver optical power monitored via SFP+ Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM / SFF-8472) to prevent receiver saturation.
limitations: Single-mode laser transceivers generate higher thermal dissipation and carry a higher cost per optic than multimode optics.
Slightly higher installation precision and clean-splice verification required.

alternativesRejected.reason: Exceeds the 400m modal dispersion limit of OM4 10GBASE-SR by 6199600m; severe pulse spreading causes bit error rate (BER) collapse.
Exceeds the 100m copper channel limit by 6199900m.

routing.protocol: Hybrid Routing: Multi-Area OSPF (IGP) + External BGP (eBGP / IPsec WAN)
routing.architecture: Dual-Tier: Internal Link-State IGP (OSPF) + Inter-Domain Path-Vector (BGP-4 / RFC 4271)
rfcReferences: RFC 4364: BGP/MPLS IP Virtual Private Networks (VPNs)
RFC 4301: Security Architecture for the Internet Protocol (IPsec)
routing.technicalExplanation: For multi-site global WAN infrastructure with 4 sites and Cloud VPC integration, a hybrid routing architecture is required. Internal site networks utilize Multi-Area OSPF for fast IGP convergence. Edge routers and Cloud Virtual Private Gateways run eBGP (AS 65001 to Cloud AS 64512), enabling policy-based path control, AS_PATH loop prevention, multi-exit discriminators (MED), and controlled route redistribution at ASBR boundaries.
routing.convergenceNotes: OSPF handles millisecond internal rerouting; BGP with BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) provides 300ms failover across redundant WAN circuits and cloud tunnels.
routing.summarizationPlan: Autonomous System Boundary Routers (ASBRs) announce only aggregated supernet CIDR blocks to cloud peers and service providers, strictly filtering internal RFC 1918 departmental subnets from leaking onto untrusted transit links.

areaDesign.description: Transits internal traffic between sites and data centers.
Autonomous System peering with AWS Direct Connect / Azure ExpressRoute and Cloud VPC.

alternativesRejected.reason: OSPF cannot cross independent administrative boundaries, cannot enforce multi-hop AS path policy filters, and exposes internal link states to third-party cloud providers.

alternativesRejected.protocol: Pure BGP for all internal desktop subnets
alternativesRejected.reason: BGP lacks rapid link-state discovery and topology awareness necessary for high-density local campus switching and fast convergence.

topology.description: Enterprise WAN routers at each regional hub meshed via IPsec VPN tunnels, terminating on Cloud VPC Virtual Private Gateways.

topology.technicalJustification: With 4 international city sites and 2000 endpoints including IoT fleets, a multi-tier WAN edge architecture is required. Edge routers terminate dual Internet/MPLS uplinks, perform IPsec encryption and route redistribution between OSPF and eBGP into cloud VPCs.

coreSwitch.content:
! =====================================================================
! NetArchitect Generated Configuration
! Device: Core / Distribution Layer Switch 01
! Hostname: GLOBAL-MULTI-CLOUD-WAN-&-IOT-CORE-SW01
! Platform Assumption: Cisco Catalyst 9500 / 9300 (IOS-XE 17.9+)
! =====================================================================
version 17.9
service timestamps debug datetime msec
service timestamps log datetime msec
service password-encryption
!
hostname GLOBAL-MULTI-CLOUD-WAN-&-IOT-CORE-SW01
!
boot-start-marker
boot-end-marker
!
! Management & Security Baselines
enable secret 9 $9$PlaceholderCoreSecret$NetArchitect
!
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
aaa authorization exec default local
username netadmin privilege 15 secret 9 $9$AdminSecret$2026Net
!
ip routing
ip domain name netarchitect.internal
ip ssh version 2
ip ssh time-out 60
ip ssh authentication-retries 3
!
! Spanning Tree Protocol (IEEE 802.1w Rapid-PVST+)
! Root Bridge Primary Configuration
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
spanning-tree extend system-id
spanning-tree vlan 1-4094 priority 4096
!
! VLAN Database Definitions
vlan 999
 name QUARANTINE_NATIVE
!
vlan 10
 name Americas_Hub_&_Automated_Scanners
!
vlan 20
 name EMEA_Logistics_Operations
!
vlan 30
 name APAC_Automated_Sorting_Depot
!
vlan 40
 name Global_IoT_Telemetry_Sensors
!
vlan 50
 name Cloud_VPC_Hybrid_Services
!
vlan 99
 name Global_WAN_Infrastructure_Management
!
! 802.1Q Core Downlink Trunks to Access Layer
! Platform note: Modern Cisco Catalyst 9000 switches use IEEE 802.1Q exclusively.
! Obsolete 'switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q' command is rejected on Cat 9000 and therefore omitted.
interface range TenGigabitEthernet1/0/1 - 4
 description 10G OM4/OS2 SFP+ 802.1Q Downlink Trunks to Access Switches
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50,99
 switchport nonegotiate
 spanning-tree guard root
 no shutdown
!
! Port-Channel Inter-Switch Link (LACP - Core Redundancy)
interface Port-channel1
 description LACP Inter-Chassis Core Cross-Connect
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50,99
 no shutdown
!
interface range TenGigabitEthernet1/0/47 - 48
 description LACP Core Member Bundle
 channel-group 1 mode active
!
! Switched Virtual Interfaces (SVIs) - Default Gateways
interface Vlan10
 description SVI Gateway for Americas Hub & Automated Scanners [VLAN 10]
 ip address 10.100.0.1 255.255.252.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan20
 description SVI Gateway for EMEA Logistics Operations [VLAN 20]
 ip address 10.100.4.1 255.255.254.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan30
 description SVI Gateway for APAC Automated Sorting Depot [VLAN 30]
 ip address 10.100.6.1 255.255.254.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan40
 description SVI Gateway for Global IoT Telemetry Sensors [VLAN 40]
 ip address 10.100.8.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan50
 description SVI Gateway for Cloud VPC Hybrid Services [VLAN 50]
 ip address 10.100.9.1 255.255.255.128
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan99
 description SVI Gateway for Global WAN Infrastructure Management [VLAN 99]
 ip address 10.100.9.129 255.255.255.224
 no shutdown
!
! Dynamic Routing Protocol: OSPF Process 1
router ospf 1
 router-id 10.255.255.1
 log-adjacency-changes
 passive-interface default
 no passive-interface Vlan10
 no passive-interface Vlan20
 no passive-interface Vlan30
 no passive-interface Vlan40
 no passive-interface Vlan50
 no passive-interface Vlan99
 network 10.100.0.0 0.0.3.255 area 0
 network 10.100.4.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.100.6.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.100.8.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
 network 10.100.9.0 0.0.0.127 area 0

line con 0

line vty 0 4

edgeRouter.title: Border / Edge Router Configuration
edgeRouter.content:
! =====================================================================
! NetArchitect Generated Configuration
! Device: Border / WAN Edge Router 01
! Hostname: GLOBAL-MULTI-CLOUD-WAN-&-IOT-EDGE-RTR01
! Platform Assumption: Cisco ISR 4451 / ASR 1001-X (IOS-XE 17.9+)
! =====================================================================
version 17.9
service timestamps debug datetime msec
service timestamps log datetime msec
service password-encryption
!
hostname GLOBAL-MULTI-CLOUD-WAN-&-IOT-EDGE-RTR01
!
enable secret 9 $9$PlaceholderRtrSecret$NetArchitect
!
ip routing
ip cef
!
! Core LAN Facing Interface (Downlink to Core Switches)
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
 description Downlink to LAN Core Switch 01
 ip address 10.255.0.1 255.255.255.252
 ip ospf 1 area 0
 no shutdown
!
! WAN / Carrier Facing Interface
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 description WAN Uplink to Carrier Provider / EVPL
 ip address 198.51.100.2 255.255.255.252
 ip access-group WAN_INBOUND_FILTER in
 no shutdown
!
!
! External BGP Peering (eBGP AS 65001 to Cloud/Carrier AS 64512)
router bgp 65001
 bgp log-neighbor-changes
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 remote-as 64512
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 description Primary Carrier / Cloud VPC Gateway
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 fall-over bfd
 !
 address-family ipv4
  neighbor 198.51.100.1 activate
  neighbor 198.51.100.1 prefix-list SUMMARY_ONLY out
  network 10.100.0.0 mask 255.255.252.0
 exit-address-family
!
!
! Internal Dynamic Routing: OSPF Process 1
router ospf 1
 router-id 10.255.255.254
 log-adjacency-changes
 passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 network 10.100.0.0 0.0.3.255 area 0
 network 10.100.4.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.100.6.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.100.8.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
 network 10.100.9.0 0.0.0.127 area 0
 network 10.100.9.128 0.0.0.31 area 0
!
! Static Default Route to Carrier Gateway
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 198.51.100.1
!
! WAN Edge Security Filter
ip access-list extended WAN_INBOUND_FILTER
 remark Block Inbound RFC 1918 Private Addresses (Anti-Spoofing)
 deny ip 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 any
 deny ip 172.16.0.0 0.15.255.255 any
 deny ip 192.168.0.0 0.0.255.255 any
 remark Permit Established State Sessions
 permit tcp any any established
 remark Permit Essential ICMP Diagnostics
 permit icmp any any echo-reply
 permit icmp any any unreachable
 permit icmp any any time-exceeded
 remark Permit IPsec VPN Tunnels
 permit esp any host 198.51.100.2
 permit udp any host 198.51.100.2 eq isakmp
 permit udp any host 198.51.100.2 eq non500-isakmp
 remark Deny All Other Inbound Traffic
 deny ip any any log
!
end
write memory

explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Rule 5.C: Distance > 400m -> OS2 Single-Mode Fiber (9/125 µm core)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Distance 6200000m exceeds 400m multimode modal dispersion boundary by 6199600m. Single-mode zero-modal dispersion required.
explanations.technicalExplanation: For link distances above 400m (6200.0 km requested), OS2 Single-Mode Fiber (9/125 µm core) eliminates modal dispersion entirely. Core diameter permits only a single fundamental transverse optical mode, enabling high-bandwidth transmission over tens of kilometers. Interface "10GBASE-ZR SFP+ (1550nm Cooled EML / APD Receiver)" was selected to guarantee optical link margin over the required span.

alternativesRejected.reason: Exceeds the 400m modal dispersion limit of OM4 10GBASE-SR by 6199600m; severe pulse spreading causes bit error rate (BER) collapse.
Exceeds the 100m copper channel limit by 6199900m.

assumptions: Low water-peak ITU-T G.652.D single-mode fiber infrastructure.
Optical attenuation calculated at 1310nm (~0.35-0.4 dB/km) or 1550nm (~0.22-0.25 dB/km).
Receiver optical power monitored via SFP+ Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM / SFF-8472) to prevent receiver saturation.
warnings: Distance exceeds 80 km without optical amplification (EDFA) or dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM).

explanations.decision: Selected Optical Interface: 10GBASE-ZR SFP+ (1550nm Cooled EML / APD Receiver)

inputParameters.connectorType: LC Duplex (or SC/APC for Carrier Telco Hand-off)

explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Transceiver Reach Selection vs Optical Power Budgeting
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Total Power Budget = Min Launch Power (0 dBm) - Max Rx Sensitivity (-24 dBm) = 24 dB. Channel Insertion Loss = Fiber Loss (6200 km x 0.22 dB/km = 1364 dB) + Connector Loss (2 dB) + Splice Loss (1 dB) = 1367 dB. Calculated Net Optical Margin = 24 dB - 1367 dB = -1343 dB (Negative Margin - Amplification Required).
explanations.technicalExplanation: The transceiver module was selected based on transmitter launch power, photodetector sensitivity, dispersion penalty over distance, and operating wavelength (1550 nm (Cooled Narrow-Linewidth Laser)). Selecting higher-powered optics (such as ZR on a short link) could saturate the optical receiver diode, while insufficient optics would fail bit-error-rate thresholds.

alternativesRejected.reason: Lacks modularity; SFP+ allows field replacement and sparing flexibility.

assumptions: Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM/SFF-8472) enabled on all optical transceivers.
Receiver dynamic range is not exceeded; attenuators installed if power exceeds max receiver input.
warnings: Extended reach 1550nm optics require APD receiver verification to avoid overload.

explanations.decision: Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM) Allocations for 6 Departments
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Descending-Order Binary Radix Tree Subnet Allocation (RFC 4632 / CIDR)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Root Network: 10.100.0.0/19 contains 8192 total IP addresses. Allocated: 2464 addresses across 6 subnets. Address Space Utilization: 30.1%. Remaining Free Space: 5728 addresses.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Subnet requests were sorted strictly in descending order of host requirements prior to allocation. This deterministic ordering prevents memory fragmentation and guarantees that every allocated subnet starts on a naturally aligned binary address boundary (where starting address mod 2^(32 - prefix) == 0). Network and broadcast addresses are mathematically preserved, preventing subnet overlap or silent address overflow.
explanations.standardsReference: RFC 4632 (Classless Inter-domain Routing) & RFC 1918 (Private Address Allocation)

alternativesRejected.technology: Classful Subnetting (FLSM / Fixed Length Subnet Masking)
alternativesRejected.reason: Forces uniform mask (e.g. /25 for all departments), causing severe address exhaustion and waste for small departments.
Causes address fragmentation where larger blocks cannot find continuous aligned binary boundaries.

assumptions: Standard LAN segments reserve 2 addresses (Network ID and Directed Broadcast).
The first usable IPv4 address in each subnet is designated as the Default Gateway (SVI).

explanations.decision: Selected Hybrid Routing: Multi-Area OSPF (IGP) + External BGP (eBGP / IPsec WAN)

inputParameters.architecture: Dual-Tier: Internal Link-State IGP (OSPF) + Inter-Domain Path-Vector (BGP-4 / RFC 4271)

explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Dijkstra SPF Shortest-Path First Link-State Routing with Area Hierarchies
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: SPF Time Complexity: O(E + V log V) where V = 12 nodes, E = 20 links. Database scale remains well within sub-second Dijkstra recomputation limits (<15ms compute overhead).
explanations.technicalExplanation: For multi-site global WAN infrastructure with 4 sites and Cloud VPC integration, a hybrid routing architecture is required. Internal site networks utilize Multi-Area OSPF for fast IGP convergence. Edge routers and Cloud Virtual Private Gateways run eBGP (AS 65001 to Cloud AS 64512), enabling policy-based path control, AS_PATH loop prevention, multi-exit discriminators (MED), and controlled route redistribution at ASBR boundaries.

alternativesRejected.reason: OSPF cannot cross independent administrative boundaries, cannot enforce multi-hop AS path policy filters, and exposes internal link states to third-party cloud providers.

alternativesRejected.protocol: Pure BGP for all internal desktop subnets
alternativesRejected.reason: BGP lacks rapid link-state discovery and topology awareness necessary for high-density local campus switching and fast convergence.

assumptions: All OSPF Area 0 routers maintain contiguous backbone adjacencies.
Point-to-point OSPF network type configured on all routed inter-switch links to bypass DR/BDR election latency.

explanations.decision: IEEE 802.1w Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (Rapid-PVST+) & 802.1Q Tagged Trunks
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol Proposal-Agreement Handshake (RFC 802.1w)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Convergence time reduced from 30-50 seconds (Legacy 802.1D Spanning Tree) to < 1.0 second (802.1w Rapid-PVST+) via direct edge-port PortFast transitions and point-to-point proposal-agreement handshakes.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Rapid-PVST+ is configured with explicit bridge priority tuning. Core Switch 01 is configured with Priority 4096 (Root Primary), and Core Switch 02 with Priority 8192 (Root Secondary). Access switches use default 32768. BPDU Guard is enabled on all access edge ports to instantly error-disable ports if rogue switches are attached, preventing accidental root bridge takeover. Native VLAN is changed to an unused quarantine VLAN 999 to mitigate VLAN hopping attacks.

alternativesRejected.reason: Slow 30 to 50 second convergence timers (Listening and Learning states) disrupt mission-critical traffic and VoIP streams.
Leaves trunk open to VLAN hopping and unauthorized broadcast domain leakage; native VLAN 1 presents documented security vulnerabilities.

assumptions: Uplink interfaces configured as Point-to-Point full-duplex to enable RSTP rapid transitions.
BPDU Guard enabled globally on all PortFast access ports.

explanations.decision: Strict Priority Low-Latency Queuing (LLQ) with Sub-5ms Target Analysis
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Fiber Optical Time of Flight (ToF) & Differentiated Services (DiffServ / RFC 2474)
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: Light propagation in silica fiber core (refractive index n ≈ 1.468): v = c / n = 299,792 km/s / 1.4682 ≈ 204,190 km/s (4.898 µs/km). One-way fiber flight delay for 6200 km = 30367.60 µs. Round-Trip Time (RTT) pure fiber propagation = 60.735 ms. Remaining latency budget for switch serialization, queuing, and carrier transport: -55.735 ms.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Do NOT guarantee sub-5ms latency merely because QoS is enabled! Latency is governed by fundamental physics and carrier transport. While the pure optical propagation delay across 6200 km is 60.735 ms, the total end-to-end latency experienced depends on: (1) Carrier route curvature/trench routing factor (typically 1.3x - 1.5x physical distance), (2) DWDM optical transponder regeneration, (3) Buffer queuing delays, and (4) Store-and-forward switch serialization delay. QoS Low-Latency Queuing (LLQ / Expedited Forwarding DSCP 46) eliminates queuing jitter for voice and high-priority financial packets, but cannot reduce the physical optical propagation constant.
explanations.standardsReference: RFC 2474 (DiffServ Architecture), RFC 3246 (Expedited Forwarding PHB), ITU-T G.8261

alternativesRejected.reason: Large bulk file transfers induce bufferbloat, increasing latency spikes well above 20-50ms.

assumptions: Carrier EVPL path does not exceed 1.4x straight-line fiber trench distance.
Core interfaces run at 10Gbps line-rate with hardware cut-through or fast store-and-forward switching.
warnings: Sub-5ms latency SLA requires strict carrier SLA commitments and verification via RFC 2544 / ITU-T Y.1564 BERT testing; QoS configuration alone cannot overcome transmission distance.

explanations.decision: IPsec AES-256-GCM / IKEv2 Cryptographic Tunneling & eBGP Peering
explanations.appliedAlgorithm: Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) & BGP Route Filtering
explanations.mathematicalCalculation: IPsec encapsulation overhead: 20 bytes IPv4 + 8 bytes ESP + 16 bytes IV/ICV = ~56 bytes per packet. WAN MTU adjusted to 1440 bytes with TCP MSS clamping at 1400 bytes to prevent packet fragmentation.
explanations.technicalExplanation: Site-to-site communication traversing public networks or carrier infrastructure is encrypted via IPsec using IKEv2 and modern AES-256-GCM. eBGP peers exchange only verified summary prefix-lists. Anti-spoofing ACLs drop inbound RFC 1918 traffic arriving on external interfaces (BCP 38 / RFC 2827).
explanations.standardsReference: RFC 4301 (IPsec Security Architecture), RFC 7296 (IKEv2), RFC 2827 (Network Ingress Filtering / BCP 38)

alternativesRejected.reason: Transmits all corporate and IoT payloads in plaintext across public transit networks.
Cryptographically broken; susceptible to Sweet32 collision attacks and collision vulnerabilities.

assumptions: Cloud VPC Virtual Private Gateway configured with ASN 64512.
TCP MSS Clamping enabled on all crypto tunnel interfaces to prevent PMTU black holes.

decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Rule 5.C: Distance > 400m -> OS2 Single-Mode Fiber (9/125 µm core)
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Distance 6200000m exceeds 400m multimode modal dispersion boundary by 6199600m. Single-mode zero-modal dispersion required.
decisions.technicalExplanation: For link distances above 400m (6200.0 km requested), OS2 Single-Mode Fiber (9/125 µm core) eliminates modal dispersion entirely. Core diameter permits only a single fundamental transverse optical mode, enabling high-bandwidth transmission over tens of kilometers. Interface "10GBASE-ZR SFP+ (1550nm Cooled EML / APD Receiver)" was selected to guarantee optical link margin over the required span.

alternativesRejected.reason: Exceeds the 400m modal dispersion limit of OM4 10GBASE-SR by 6199600m; severe pulse spreading causes bit error rate (BER) collapse.
Exceeds the 100m copper channel limit by 6199900m.

assumptions: Low water-peak ITU-T G.652.D single-mode fiber infrastructure.
Optical attenuation calculated at 1310nm (~0.35-0.4 dB/km) or 1550nm (~0.22-0.25 dB/km).
Receiver optical power monitored via SFP+ Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM / SFF-8472) to prevent receiver saturation.
warnings: Distance exceeds 80 km without optical amplification (EDFA) or dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM).

decisions.decision: Selected Optical Interface: 10GBASE-ZR SFP+ (1550nm Cooled EML / APD Receiver)

inputParameters.connectorType: LC Duplex (or SC/APC for Carrier Telco Hand-off)

decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Transceiver Reach Selection vs Optical Power Budgeting
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Total Power Budget = Min Launch Power (0 dBm) - Max Rx Sensitivity (-24 dBm) = 24 dB. Channel Insertion Loss = Fiber Loss (6200 km x 0.22 dB/km = 1364 dB) + Connector Loss (2 dB) + Splice Loss (1 dB) = 1367 dB. Calculated Net Optical Margin = 24 dB - 1367 dB = -1343 dB (Negative Margin - Amplification Required).
decisions.technicalExplanation: The transceiver module was selected based on transmitter launch power, photodetector sensitivity, dispersion penalty over distance, and operating wavelength (1550 nm (Cooled Narrow-Linewidth Laser)). Selecting higher-powered optics (such as ZR on a short link) could saturate the optical receiver diode, while insufficient optics would fail bit-error-rate thresholds.

alternativesRejected.reason: Lacks modularity; SFP+ allows field replacement and sparing flexibility.

assumptions: Digital Optical Monitoring (DOM/SFF-8472) enabled on all optical transceivers.
Receiver dynamic range is not exceeded; attenuators installed if power exceeds max receiver input.
warnings: Extended reach 1550nm optics require APD receiver verification to avoid overload.

decisions.decision: Variable Length Subnet Mask (VLSM) Allocations for 6 Departments
decisions.appliedAlgorithm: Descending-Order Binary Radix Tree Subnet Allocation (RFC 4632 / CIDR)
decisions.mathematicalCalculation: Root Network: 10.100.0.0/19 contains 8192 total IP addresses. Allocated: 2464 addresses across 6 subnets. Address Space Utilization: 30.1%. Remaining Free Space: 5728 addresses.
decisions.technicalExplanation: Subnet requests were sorted strictly in descending order of host requirements prior to allocation. This deterministic ordering prevents memory fragmentation and guarantees that every allocated subnet starts on a naturally aligned binary address boundary (where starting address mod 2^(32 - prefix) == 0). Network and broadcast addresses are mathematically preserved, preventing subnet overlap or silent address overflow.
decisions.standardsReference: RFC 4632 (Classless Inter-domain Routing) & RFC 1918 (Private Address Allocation)

alternativesRejected.technology: Classful Subnetting (FLSM / Fixed Length Subnet Masking)
alternativesRejected.reason: Forces uniform mask (e.g. /25 for all departments), causing severe address exhaustion and waste for small departments.
Causes address fragmentation where larger blocks cannot find continuous aligned binary boundaries.

assumptions: Standard LAN segments reserve 2 addresses (Network ID and Directed Broadcast).
The first usable IPv4 address in each subnet is designated as the Default Gateway (SVI).
